rmk:
There is a normal kong-a-ree from another rwbl, but I was after the whistled wheee! at about 3khz. I was watching the bird, about 20m away at the top of a leafless cypress. This bird has been giving this unusual call for a couple of years along this stretch of the lake between the end of Cedardale and the end of Ferndale. The bird would puff its chest, spread its shoulders but not its wings, open its tail slightly, and give this loud whistled call over and over again. It was not making any of the other calls in this recording.

rmk: Bird was perched in a small bare tree at the edge of the marsh, where only the boardwalk separates the marsh from Lake Michigan.  It allowed me to come very close when I went past the first time and photographed it.  On the way back, it was agitated, I think by two motorboats that were approaching.  It started with its Chuk-type calls, then, as the boats got closer, switched to a Seer-type alarm call and flew away at 39 seconds into the recording.  Most of the Red-wings have left this marsh, and I counted only two today.  Its plumage was scruffy, but it still had its epaulet.
